#KilalaninAngPinas 𝗪𝗢𝗩𝗘𝗡 𝗕𝗬 𝗧𝗥𝗢𝗣𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗖𝗬𝗖𝗟𝗢𝗡𝗘𝗦 🌀 

The Philippines lies in the busiest region in the world in terms of tropical cyclone activity. Here's a map showing those TC tracks that crossed the Philippine archipelago since 1964. What can you notice? 

According to PAGASA, the Philippines experiences around 8-9 tropical cyclone (#bagyo) landfalls each year. The density of these land-crossing tropical cyclone tracks is evident in the regions of Luzon and Visayas, even without a map outline.

On average, 20 tropical cyclones (bagyo) form or enter the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) annually, with about 8-9 making landfall. These landfalling cyclones, especially the intense ones, often leave significant destruction in their wake.

Over the past 50 years, the Philippine archipelago has been crossed by numerous tropical cyclones, ranging from minor tropical depressions to record-breaking super typhoons. The deadliest of these was Typhoon YOLANDA (international name: HAIYAN), which claimed over 6,200 lives when it crossed the central Philippines on November 8, 2013. It is also one of the strongest landfalling tropical cyclones in the country and globally, with 10-minute maximum sustained winds exceeding 117 knots (215 kilometers per hour) near the center at landfall in the Eastern Visayas region, as recorded by the Japan Meteorological Agency.

The density of land-crossing tropical cyclone tracks in Luzon and Visayas is notable even without a map outline. Although Mindanao is less frequently hit by tropical cyclones, it has experienced several, with Typhoon Pablo (international name: BOPHA) being the strongest when it crossed the island in December 2012. 

It's important to remember that tropical cyclones don’t need to directly cross a province to cause damage. There have been instances where the outer circulation of tropical cyclones or enhanced monsoons has triggered landslides and flooding. #Kalayaan2025 #MakeItHistoric #NationalFlagDays
